title: Ice Cream 1.5L

drivers.name: Store closed Monday
drivers.evidence: Store closure removes 1/7 of weekly sales; no prior closure data, but a single day loss is 14% of weekly volume.

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Past price hikes above 2% show no uplift; demand elasticity suggests ~2% decline per 1% price rise; conservative estimate for 2.3% increase.

drivers.name: Thanksgiving (event week)
drivers.evidence: 2025: x0.95 vs baseline; noise-adjusted x1.0, but prior data suggests a 5% demand dip during the holiday week.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 44.2. Thanksgiving (event week) has a noise-adjusted effect of x1.0, but the 2025 data shows x0.95, suggesting a slight demand dip. The store is closed Monday, removing one day of sales (≈14% of week). The price is up 2.3%, which suppresses demand; past 10%+ price hikes show no lift. No promotion is scheduled. The classical model suggests x1.0, but the closed day and price increase justify downward adjustment. Evidence is limited (one past Thanksgiving, one closure), so shrink toward 1.0. No promotion lift expected. The 2024 Thanksgiving week had a promotion, so its x0.5 is not representative. Final adjustment: mild downside.

  events: Holiday: Thanksgiving (Thu)
  shelf price: 6.56 (+2.3% vs regular price 6.41)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 44.2 | 5%-95%: 11.7 - 74.8 | 10%-90%: 20.3 - 70.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-36% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
